blocks.text: Strangers who join the church are regarded as newcomers. As they grow spiritually, they climb the ranks from the bottom: newcomers move to non-baptised members, then to baptised members, who become workers-in-training, and eventually fully-fledged workers. It's from among the workers that Deacons and Deaconesses are ordained, and from there, the progression continues from Deacons/Deaconesses to Assistant Pastors, and from Assistant Pastors to Pastors, and so on.

Beyond exceptional character, spiritual endowment, and evangelistic ability, a worker being considered for ordination or promotion is required to have attended the School of Disciples, the School of Missions/Bible College, and any other major programmes the Mission specifies.
